name: Waterproofing / Tanking (Wet Areas, Roofs, Below-Grade, Balconies)
zones: plant rooms / wet risers / tank rooms

activities: surface cleaned, sound, cured and dry to spec
sequence.note: Waterproofing is only as good as the substrate falls and the wall-floor cove; standing-water areas fail first.

activities: floor gullies, puddle flanges, drain bodies set to level
sequence.note: Every penetration through the tanking must be installed BEFORE the membrane so the membrane can be dressed and sealed to it.

activities: reinforcing tape/fabric to junctions, corners, drains
apply liquid/sheet membrane to floor and wall upstand height
dress into gullies and around penetrations
sequence.note: Wall upstand height must exceed the wet zone (shower/splash) and meet code; skimping the upstand is the classic leak path.
No following trade may cover the membrane until the flood test passes and is signed; this is the single most important hold-point in wet-area finishing.

activities: controlled handover to tiling with membrane protected
sequence.note: The membrane is fragile; it must be protected from foot traffic, dropped tools and follow-on screed/tiling.

typical_relationships.before: substrate screed to falls + coving cured
typical_relationships.reason: membrane laid on flat/ponding or green substrate ponds water and debonds

typical_relationships.before: drainage & penetration first fix (gullies, flanges, sleeves)
typical_relationships.reason: the membrane must be terminated and sealed into every drain and penetration; adding penetrations after tanking punctures it
tiling over untested or uncured tanking hides defects and forces demolition of finished tiles to fix a leak
unprotected membrane is punctured by follow-on trades before it is covered
the tanking envelope must be continuous and undamaged before it disappears under finishes

interfaces.requirement: floor gullies, puddle flanges, drain bodies and pipe penetrations set to level and sealed BEFORE membrane, so the membrane is dressed and bonded to them (critical architecture-MEP handshake)
membrane fully cured and flood-tested (signed) and protected before tiling starts; tile bed adhesive compatible with membrane
substrate laid to falls, coved and cured before membrane; wet-area walls use cementitious (not gypsum) background
membrane protected from puncture and traffic; any later penetration re-detailed and re-tested, never simply drilled through
no fixing screws/anchors penetrate the tanking envelope in wet zones without approved sealed detail

commissioning_dependencies: flood/water test witnessed and signed before cover-up
integrity re-test after any later penetration
testing_requirements: flood / ponding test 24-48h with drop check
wet-film / dry-film thickness of liquid membrane
seam/overlap peel test on sheet systems
typical_exceptions: below-grade tanking is a structural-waterproofing package coordinated with civil, not a fit-out trade
pre-formed shower trays/pods reduce site-applied tanking to junctions only
integral crystalline/admixture waterproofing in the concrete replaces some applied membrane but junctions still need detailing
roof/terrace membranes tie into facade and drainage, widening the interface set

work_packages.note: gated by plumbing first fix; flood test hold-point

evidence: Waterproofing isolated as its own interface-critical pattern because it sits between plumbing first fix and tiling with a mandatory flood-test hold-point - the highest-consequence, most-litigated wet-area sequence in building finishing. Penetrations-before-membrane and protect-from-following-trades are universal rules. Generalized, non-project-specific.
